The Story

The story they didn't expect

01
Mbutho
A boy from a small village in the Eastern Cape, born into a future the system had already decided for him. No electricity, no paved roads, no permission.
02
Leaving
He left home to find work, carrying nothing but the resolve not to accept the place he'd been given.
03
Underground
He became a miner — coal dust, rock and risk, in the place where the country's wealth is dug and its workers are counted last.
04
Cost-Plus
Inside the mine's cost-plus structure, he rose from general worker to shop steward, and into union leadership.
05
Whistleblower
A union leader who became a whistleblower, speaking truth to power about State Capture when it was dangerous to do so.
06
Buying the Mine
When Arnot Mine faced closure, he and 1,029 mineworkers chose ownership over retrenchment — not a rescue, not a handout.
07
Home
What ownership actually cost, and what he carried back to Mbutho when the fight was over.
Why This Book Matters

Five questions the book asks

Truth
What happens when someone refuses to stay silent?
Leadership
What does leadership look like when people's livelihoods are at stake?
Ownership
What does economic empowerment actually cost?
Resilience
How do you rebuild after losing everything?
Legacy
What do you leave behind when the fight is over?
02 — The Author

Mxolisi Hoboyi

Born in Mbutho village, in the O.R. Tambo District Municipality of the Eastern Cape, Mxolisi Hoboyi rose from humble beginnings to become a respected union leader, whistleblower and mine owner.

He champions worker ownership, ethical leadership and economic justice. He is a husband, father and man of faith who refused to accept the place the system gave him.

Foreword by Frans Baleni

"And together with 1,029 mineworkers, he did the unthinkable — bought a mine."
